Demanded
dē-mand´ĕd
v. (asked with authority; questioned; rendering Hebrew sha'al, Aramaic she'el, Greek punthanomai and eperotao)
Latin demandare, to entrust, through Old French demander, to ask. In the AV the word is a question put by a superior — a king, a captain, or God.

Biblical Definition

God out of the whirlwind: “Gird up now thy loins like a man; for I will demand of thee, and answer thou me” (Job 38:3; 40:7), and Job at the end: “I will demand of thee, and declare thou unto me” (Job 42:4). Herod “demanded of them where Christ should be born” (Mat 2:4). The soldiers “demanded of him, saying, And what shall we do?” (Luk 3:14). The Lord “was demanded of the Pharisees, when the kingdom of God should come” (Luk 17:20). Nebuchadnezzar's secret “which the king hath demanded” no wise man could show (Dan 2:27). David “demanded of” Uriah how the war went (2Sa 11:7). The chief captain “demanded who he was, and what he had done” (Act 21:33).

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines demand as to ask or call for as one who has a claim or right; to require; to ask by authority; to question.

expand to see more

DEMAND, v.t. To ask or call for, as one who has a claim or right to receive what is sought.

2. To require as necessary or useful.

3. To ask by authority; to question; to interrogate.

Key Scripture

Job 38:3 — "Gird up now thy loins like a man; for I will demand of thee, and answer thou me."

Job 42:4 — "Hear, I beseech thee, and I will speak: I will demand of thee, and declare thou unto me."

Mat 2:4 — "And when he had gathered all the chief priests and scribes of the people together, he demanded of them where Christ should be born."

Luk 3:14 — "And the soldiers likewise demanded of him, saying, And what shall we do? And he said unto them, Do violence to no man, neither accuse any falsely; and be content with your wages."

Luk 17:20 — "And when he was demanded of the Pharisees, when the kingdom of God should come, he answered them and said, The kingdom of God cometh not with observation:"

Dan 2:27 — "Daniel answered in the presence of the king, and said, The secret which the king hath demanded cannot the wise men, the astrologers, the magicians, the soothsayers, shew unto the king;"

Modern Corruption

Man demands of God and calls it honest wrestling, and the book of Job ends with God demanding of man and man putting his hand on his mouth.

expand to see more

Job spent thirty chapters demanding an audience — “Oh that I knew where I might find him!… I would order my cause before him” — and when the audience came, the first words out of the whirlwind reversed the courtroom: I will demand of thee, and answer thou me. What followed was not an explanation of Job's sufferings but seventy questions about the foundations of the earth, and Job's reply was a hand on his mouth. The modern posture of demanding an account from God is admired as authenticity; the book that gives it the fullest hearing ends by turning the demand round. Herod's demand is the other warning: he asked the right question of the right people and got the right answer — Bethlehem — and used it to plan a massacre. A correct answer demanded for a wrong reason is worse than ignorance.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew sha'al (H7592), to ask, enquire, demand; Aramaic she'el (H7593), to ask; Greek punthanomai (G4441), to enquire; eperotao (G1905), to question.

expand to see more

Hebrew sha'al (H7592) — to ask, demand; Job 38:3, 40:7, 42:4, 2 Samuel 11:7; Aramaic she'el (H7593), Daniel 2:27.

Greek punthanomai (G4441) — to enquire, demand; Matthew 2:4, Acts 21:33; eperotao (G1905), Luke 3:14, 17:20.

Usage

"“I will demand of thee, and answer thou me” — the courtroom reversed."

"“Demanded of them where Christ should be born” — the right answer for a massacre."

"“The soldiers likewise demanded of him, saying, And what shall we do?” — an honest demand, honestly answered."
